purpose: Classify pull-request integration gates so a green, mergeable, authorized PR is merged instead of being mislabeled as a blocker, then route normal consumers to the canonical default branch after merge.
merge_now_when: pull request is open and not already merged
every repository-required check conclusion is success
unresolved review finding count is zero
true_blockers: pull request is closed without merge
a repository-required check is not successful
merge authority is unavailable when merge intent exists
required_merge_action: Merge immediately with expected-head protection, then verify the canonical default branch advanced to a commit containing the merged head before declaring integration complete.

rules: After merge, normal consumers must be routed to the canonical default branch or its registered public artifact, not instructed to fetch the merged feature branch.
Feature-branch retrieval after merge is allowed only for explicit historical, forensic, or branch-specific debugging intent.
A post-merge handoff must record the merge commit or verified default-branch commit before claiming mainline availability.

forbidden_outcomes: reporting a green mergeable merge-authorized PR as a blocker
stopping at PR review or PR status when merge is authorized and every merge gate is satisfied
asking the operator for permission to merge when merge authority and merge intent are already explicit
telling normal users to fetch or pin a feature branch after that work has been merged to the canonical default branch
claiming integration complete without verifying the default branch advanced
merging when required checks, review findings, mergeability, expected-head identity, or authority remain unresolved
proof_ceiling: The contract and classifier prove deterministic merge-gate classification and post-merge handoff rules for supplied PR state. Actual provider merge success and default-branch advancement require observed Git/GitHub evidence.
